description: Least-privilege permission model for the coding harness. Policy as code: read by agent-guard.cjs, policy-guard.cjs and tool-output-guard.cjs through permission-engine.cjs, checked by validate-permissions.mjs, and rendered into docs/security/PERMISSION-MODEL.md. A Markdown document alone enforces nothing; docs/security/ENFORCEMENT-STATUS.md says which statements are enforced and which still depend on human procedure.

P0.name: Read local project files and approved documentation

P1.name: Modify local code and execute safe tests
P1.approval: none; bounded by the agent's write scope and command allow-list

P2.name: Modify Git branches and create pull requests
P2.approval: signed approval, plus repository-policy compliance checked by CI

P3.name: Modify approved non-production Azure resources
P3.approval: explicit signed approval naming an approved scope

P4.name: Sensitive infrastructure, data or security operations
P4.approval: separate P4 authorization by distinct approvers; never satisfied by a generic approval

local-fs.description: Files in the working copy and the local temp area

local-exec.description: Commands run on the developer machine

github-remote.description: The GitHub repository, pull requests and workflow runs

external-docs.description: Approved public documentation hosts and servers

azure-nonprod.description: Approved non-production Azure subscription and resource groups (none exist; D-037 open)

azure-prod.description: Any production Azure scope. No agent may ever hold a ceiling here (HC-11)

agentCeilingNote: An environment that is absent means no access at all. No agent has a ceiling for azure-nonprod or azure-prod, so every Azure operation is denied. The validator derives each ceiling from agent-policy.json (tools, commands, MCP grants) and fails if the two disagree.

unscopedSession.description: A Copilot session that is not a named specialist agent (for example the default agent used by a human). It has no agent identity, so tier ceilings and deny-unknown cannot be applied. The repository-wide guard still enforces the non-negotiable denials below. Use a specialist agent for any task that matters.

fs.read.description: Read a file or list a folder

meta.description: Session housekeeping (intent, todo, skill, ask the user)

agent.delegate.description: Hand a task to another agent. Never transfers approvals or ceilings

gh.read.description: gh pr and run list, view, checks

docs.read.description: Approved documentation host or documentation MCP server

azure.nonprod.read.description: Read non-production Azure state. Needs a ceiling and a signed-in identity; neither exists

fs.write.description: Write a file inside the agent's own write scope

exec.test.description: Run the repository's own tests and validators

git.write.description: Stage, commit, branch, tag, merge, rebase or reset locally

pr.write.description: Create, edit, comment on or review a pull request

azure.nonprod.write.description: Create or update a non-production Azure resource

azure.nonprod.deploy.description: Deploy reviewed infrastructure to non-production (azd, deployment create, terraform apply)

azure.delete.description: Delete, purge or destroy any Azure or cluster resource

azure.rbac.write.description: Create or change role assignments, identities or directory objects

azure.policy.write.description: Change policy, network security or firewall configuration

secret.read.description: Read a secret, key, token or credential file

secret.write.description: Create or change a secret or credential file

azure.secret.read.description: Read or list Azure secrets, keys, tokens or connection strings

data.cross-shipowner.description: Read or disclose one shipowner's data while acting for another

data.cross-jurisdiction.description: Move, copy or send jurisdiction-bound data across a jurisdiction boundary or off the machine

regulatory.file.description: Submit a certification or regulatory filing

commercial.settle.description: Settle, pay or finalise a commercial dispute, claim or invoice

git.protected.modify.description: Push or merge to a protected branch, force-push, delete a branch or rewrite history

control-plane.write.description: Change hooks, policy, approvals, approver keys, audit logs, workflows or scripts

fs.write.executable.description: Write an executable or script file outside a phase-enabled code scope. Closes the write-then-run route

shell.indirection.description: A shell command built or hidden at run time (variables joined into a command name, Invoke-Expression, encoded commands, nested shells, inline interpreters, npx). Its real target cannot be classified, so it is refused

neverGrantableNote: No approval of any tier can authorise these for an agent. A human performs them directly, outside the agent, under the break-glass or release procedure. A P4 approval can authorise only the P4 operations that are not listed here: azure.delete, azure.rbac.write, azure.policy.write, fs.write.executable.
scopeNote: The human sets these two variables in the shell before starting a session. An agent cannot change the environment of the process that runs the hooks. With a variable unset, every path of that class is denied.

defaults.statement: Read-only unless additional access is justified
Deny unknown tools and unknown operations
enforcement: engine: an unclassified command is an unknown operation and is denied for named agents
engine: jurisdiction path class, session scope, two-jurisdiction rule, egress rule
engine: shipowner path class, session scope, two-owner rule
output filter removes other owners' lines from search results

defaults.statement: Deny secret extraction and credential exposure
enforcement: engine and policy-guard: secret path class, azure.secret.read

defaults.statement: Deny destructive cloud operations by default
enforcement: engine and policy-guard: azure.delete is P4 and never reachable by a generic approval
no agent has an Azure ceiling

defaults.statement: Deny modification of protected branches without the approved workflow
enforcement: engine: git.protected.modify is never grantable to an agent

defaults.statement: Deny deployment of unreviewed infrastructure changes
enforcement: engine: azure.nonprod.deploy needs a signed approval bound to the reviewed commit

defaults.statement: Deny autonomous regulatory filings and commercial settlements
enforcement: engine: regulatory.file and commercial.settle are never grantable to an agent

approvals.limitsNote: Lifetimes, use counts and approver counts are proposed values set by this design for the owner to confirm. They are not derived from any external requirement.
rules: An approval names exact agents, exact operations and an environment. A wildcard is never accepted
An approval for a lower tier is never accepted for a higher-tier operation, even if it lists that operation
P4 approvals must name each operation explicitly and need signatures from distinct registered approvers who hold the P4 capability
An approval for one agent is not valid for another: delegation transfers nothing
P3 deployment approvals are bound to the reviewed Git commit; the request must run at that commit
An approval is rejected if it is unsigned, signed by an unregistered or revoked key, altered, expired, not yet valid, out of scope or used up
Agents cannot write the approvals folder or the approver registry (control-plane write is never grantable)

P2.name: Git branch and pull request changes
steps: A human or CI-required reviewer states the branch pattern and operations in an approval request
A registered approver signs it (approval.mjs sign) after reading the request
The agent works only on branches matching the approval, never on a protected branch
A pull request is opened; CI must pass npm run validate and npm test (repository-policy compliance)
A human reviews and merges through GitHub. Agents never merge
enforcedBy: signed approval verified by the hook
CI gate on the pull request
branch protection (specified; unavailable on this plan, see ENFORCEMENT-STATUS)

P3.name: Non-production Azure change
steps: The change exists as reviewed infrastructure code at a specific commit with a recorded what-if result
The approval request names the agent, operations, subscription and resource group, and the commit
A registered approver signs it; lifetime and use count are limited
The agent uses a scoped Azure identity whose Azure RBAC role and scope match the approval (specified, not created)
The result is recorded as evidence by the recorder; the denied and allowed actions are in the audit log

P4.name: Sensitive infrastructure, data or security operation
steps: A separate P4 request names each operation, the reason and the rollback plan
Two distinct registered approvers with the P4 capability sign it; a generic approval cannot substitute
Lifetime is short and single use
A post-action review is recorded within one working day (human procedure)
enforcedBy: signature and tier checks in the engine

breakGlass.purpose: Restore service or contain an incident when the normal workflow cannot be followed in time. Used by a human, not by an agent.
breakGlass.scope: Only operations that are not neverGrantable. A human acting directly may do more, under their own credentials, outside the agent.
requires: a recorded reason and incident or change reference
two distinct registered P4 approvers for any agent-run operation
a lifetime no longer than the P4 limit
audit marker breakGlass true on the approval
afterwards: post-incident review within one working day
add the denied and allowed actions from the audit log to the review
decide whether the normal workflow needs to change
enforcedBy: engine treats a break-glass approval as a P4 approval with extra checks
